producer_report.summary:
I added `athena land <job> --pr`. It pushes the job's branch, opens a pull request, waits for green checks and stores the link in the job's state directory. The new `[landing] merge_via_rest` setting is off when absent. With it off, the command stops at an open pull request and reports whether its checks are green. Running the command again later finds the merge by the stored pull request number and runs `check_merged`. The job is landed if the fingerprint matches, and `merged-unverified` otherwise. With the setting on, the REST merge call is made only when checks are green.

clippy and `cargo test --locked` pass. fmt was applied in place; I did not run `cargo fmt --all --check` itself. Every flow test uses fakes, so nothing ran against a real host or the real `gh` program.

- **`gh.rs`:** the host client runs only `gh api` with `repos/...` paths. The tests assert each call starts with `api`, uses a `repos/` path and contains no `pr` or `--auto` argument. The file contains no `graphql` text and no `@` anywhere.
- **Branch:** the job's branch is `athena/<job id>`. I chose that name because the code had no work-branch naming. The push goes through `check_push`, there is no force option, and nothing is pushed or opened if the guard refuses.
- **Setting:** `merge_via_rest` is read from `athena.toml` at HEAD and defaults to false. `athena.toml` is unchanged; a test confirms the setting reads as off without it.
- **Tests:** the fake-host tests cover the setting off, the setting on, and red or pending checks with the setting on (no merge). They also cover a later-seen merge landing or ending `merged-unverified`, and push refusals. The REST client has its own test, and `checks` and `parse_remote` are tested separately.
- **Other changes:** `pr.rs` gains a small `observe_merge`. The CLI wiring, display, README, CHANGELOG and the design doc are updated.
- **Words and emails:** I searched `gh.rs` for banned words, `@` and `graphql` and found none. I read the full diff and found no email-shaped text or banned words in it.

This is the first slice of the flow. The pull request title and body are simple (job title, verifier summary, job id), and the merge method is `merge`. Checks with no report at all count as pending, so a repository without CI never reaches green. Only a github.com remote named `origin` is supported, and stealth mode is untouched."

checks_run.command: cargo fmt --all (then cargo fmt --all --check was not run separately)
checks_run.note: fmt applied in place after the last code edit; only docs edits followed.
Clean after adding manual Debug impls for the three new public structs that hold trait objects.
All suites passed, including the new gh.rs tests and the config test.

open_issues: athena.toml is unchanged on purpose: the setting defaults to false when absent, which a test checks.
Nothing was run against a real host or the real gh program; all flow tests use fakes. gh.rs calls gh api only, and its tests assert every call starts with api and uses a repos/ path.
The PR is opened with merge_method=merge, and the title and body are simple (job title, verifier summary, job id). They are not the richer owned-mode body in the design.
Checks with no report at all count as pending, so a repository without CI never reaches green. Polling is 30 looks, 20 seconds apart, and is fixed in wiring.rs.
A remote branch the local clone does not know is refused by the push guard. The command does not fetch first.
Only github.com remotes named origin are supported. Stealth mode is not touched.
I did not run `cargo fmt --all --check` itself; I ran `cargo fmt --all` after the last code edit.
The boundary-word scan and email check were done by search on gh.rs and by reading the full diff. I found no email-shaped text, no banned words and no graphql text.
mistakes: My first draft had a merge_outcome_of helper that fabricated empty fingerprints. I removed it before finishing.
The first clippy run failed on missing Debug impls; fixed.
learnings: Config uses deny_unknown_fields, so a new table needs its own struct. A serde default on the Config field keeps athena.toml valid without edits.
Workspace clippy lints include missing_debug_implementations, so public structs holding trait objects need manual Debug impls.
The candidate commit and verified fingerprint come from the job's verification record (candidate_commit, verified_fingerprint, final_verdict). The base commit is in the candidate record.
Athena::go finds a blocked closing commit by greping the log for trailers. The new land path avoids that and uses the stored PR number only.
No work-branch naming existed in the code, so I defined athena/<job id> as the one branch the push guard allows.
desires: A Bash allowance for `cargo fmt --all --check` output, and a way to read cargo output without piping (the full test log was too large to read).
